context: Comparative data visualization — four US choropleths showing the same synthetic state income data classified by four different methods (Quantile, Equal Interval, Jenks Natural Breaks, Manual Threshold), with an interactive histogram below showing breakpoints from all methods simultaneously.
first_impression: A well-conceived educational comparison with a deliberate warm YlOrBr palette, but the cramped layout and 9px legend text undermine readability at rendered size.
what_works: The YlOrBr sequential palette is clearly intentional — light yellow to deep brown is a publication-quality choice for income data, far above schemeCategory10 defaults. The histogram with color-coded, dash-differentiated breakpoint lines from all four methods overlaid in one chart is genuinely clever and informative design.
what_doesnt: Legend items rendered at 9px monospaced font are too small to read comfortably — dollar range labels like '$36,000–$48,000' are barely legible, undermining the whole point of comparing classification schemes. Panel gap (6px vertical) and 10px description text make the overall layout feel cramped rather than confidently spaced.
